identity.title: [Mechanism research on CYLC1 deficiency-induced teratozoospermia and male fertility decline].

content.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate the impact of CYLC1 on male fertility in both humans and mice. Methods Screening of the male infertility cohort was conducted using whole-exome sequencing technology. And bioinformatic analysis (PolyPhen-2, MutationTaster and SIFT) was applied for identified mutation sites. Sperm morphology in patients was analyzed using Papanicolaou staining and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The Cylc1 gene knockout mouse model was generated using CRISPR/Cas9 technology. Semen parameters of Cylc1 homozygous knockout mice were analyzed using a Neubauer hemocytometer, followed by Papanicolaou staining. Testicular function in Cylc1 homozygous knockout mice was assessed through HE staining, PAS staining and immunofluorescence staining. ResultsMutations in the CYLC1 gene led to male teratozoospermia, primarily characterized by acrosomal structural defects. No obvious abnormalities were observed in the reproductive organs of Cylc1 homozygous knockout mice, but sperm motility and count were significantly lower than in wild-type mice. Papanicolaou staining and SEM analysis showed abnormal sperm head morphology (particularly in acrosomal development) in Cylc1 homozygous knockout mice. Further staining analysis revealed that acrosomal abnormalities were already present during the round spermatid stage in Cylc1 knockout mice and became increasingly pronounced in later stages of spermiogenesis. ConclusionCYLC1 gene mutations cause abnormal sperm head morphology, leading to male infertility. The absence of CYLC1 protein disrupts the normal formation of sperm head structures (especially the acrosome), thereby reducing the fertility of male Cylc1 knockout mice.
